multiply-cost.title: What a multiplication buys
multiply-cost.caption: Each tile is one multiplication. A sample into an arrow costs two; an arrow turned by an arrow costs four.

work-grid.title: The bill for one block
work-grid.caption: One row per bin, one column per sample. The dashed outline is what the chip finishes before the next block arrives: 25,625 of the 42,230 multiplications.

back-wheel.title: Turning back, in degrees and radians
back-wheel.caption: Back means clockwise. Each turn is written in degrees and in radians, where a full turn is 2π.

shared-arrows.title: Bins 1 and 5 share their arrows
shared-arrows.caption: Bin 1 against bin 5, sample by sample. Even samples: the same arrow. Odd samples: flipped, half a turn apart.

odd-walk.title: The odd part, by hand
odd-walk.caption: In order: 1, the odd part laid tip to tail; 2, turned back the extra 45°; 3, added to the even part for bin 1 and subtracted for bin 5.

butterfly.title: One butterfly
butterfly.caption: The even and odd results come in, the odd one is turned, and the crossing lines add it for bin 1 and subtract it for bin 5. X[k] means bin k.

split-tree.title: Splitting all the way down
split-tree.caption: Each level splits every block into its even and odd samples. The numbers count the multiplications if you stop splitting at that level.

butterfly-network.title: The 8-sample FFT
butterfly-network.caption: Read from the inputs to the bins: three layers of four butterflies, each turn labelled with the arrow it turns by. The thick butterfly is the one you computed by hand.

growth.title: The FFT’s gain grows with N
growth.caption: Both axes are on log scales: going up, each grid line is ten times the one below; going right, N doubles at each tick. The gap between the lines is how many times fewer multiplications the FFT needs.

bit-reverse.title: Bit-reversed order
bit-reverse.caption: Write each sample number in binary and read it backwards: that is the position it enters the network at.

bins-256.title: The keypad tones at N = 256
bins-256.caption: Each tone lands on its own bin with at least one empty bin between neighbors. The dashed ticks are the old 205-sample bins.

budget.title: What each split costs
budget.caption: Each bar is one choice of splits, on an ordinary axis from 0. Solid bars fit under the chip’s budget, hollow ones do not; the dotted part of each bar is the butterflies, which stay small.

wrap-wheel.title: A 4-sample DFT repeats after 4 bins
wrap-wheel.caption: Bin k turns back k × 90° per sample. Bins 4 to 7 add a full turn, which does not count, so each lands on the bin four below it.

goertzel-swing.title: Goertzel’s filter, pushed in time
goertzel-swing.caption: The pole pair and their sum, 2 × cos 35.1°, then the filter’s output, growing like a swing pushed in time, against a tone at the wrong speed.

goertzel-final.title: The last step of Goertzel
goertzel-final.caption: Take the last output, subtract the one before it turned back one step of the test wheel, and the length of the result is the bin’s match.

crossover.title: Goertzel against the FFT
crossover.caption: Goertzel pays per bin; the FFT pays once for all of them. Below about 16 bins Goertzel is cheaper.
